context.title: Blessings and Curses
context.summary: Moses lists the blessings that will follow obedience and the far longer list of curses that will follow disobedience: disease, drought, defeat, siege, famine and scattering among the nations.
context.background: Ancient treaties ended with blessings and curses on those who kept or broke them. Some curses here closely resemble those in a 7th-century BC treaty of the Assyrian king Esarhaddon, such as heaven like bronze and earth like iron (v. 23). The siege famine of verses 53–57 is later described in Samaria (2 Kings 6:28-29) and Jerusalem (Lamentations 4:10).

customs.term: The head, and not the tail
customs.note: An image of leading rather than following, of honor rather than humiliation. Verse 44 reverses it.

watchFor: The curses in vv. 16–19 mirror the blessings in vv. 3–6.
The blessings fill 14 verses; the curses, 54.
'Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness' (v. 47).

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.
